rationale: CR-001 and CR-002 resolved in current source (Step 4 now runs exists for every named non-default project; createProjectsSubcommand split into 15 register helpers, each under ~50 lines). CR-003 (ticket key in commit subjects) was intentionally not fixed and stays unresolved.

findings.title: Skill Step 4 skips exists for non-admin projects
findings.problem: Spec requires running `codemie sdk projects exists` for any named non-default project. Step 4 exempts non-admins' projects listed in `applications` and adds an 'exit 0 wins over applications' disagreement rule not in the spec (AC6 partial).
findings.impact: Required behavior of the Project Clarification flow is unmet; the skill may proceed without the existence check the spec mandates.
findings.recommendation: Make Step 4 run `exists` for every named non-default project regardless of admin status; drop the applications exemption and the extra disagreement rule, or get the spec amended.
findings.check_notes: SKILL.md line 72: exists required for any other named project; exemption and extra rule removed

fix.change: Step 4 runs exists for every named non-default project; dropped applications exemption and disagreement rule

findings.title: createProjectsSubcommand far exceeds 50 lines
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires functions under 50 lines; createProjectsSubcommand() is about 290 lines defining all subcommands inline.
findings.impact: Documented code-structure standard broken; blocks the workflow per standards review.
findings.recommendation: Split into per-subcommand registration helpers (e.g. registerListCommand(cmd)) called from createProjectsSubcommand().
findings.check_notes: 15 register* helpers plus a thin createProjectsSubcommand; no function exceeds ~50 lines

fix.change: split createProjectsSubcommand into per-command register helpers

findings.title: Ticket key suffixed on commit subjects
findings.problem: git-workflow.md lists the ticket key in the commit subject as a pitfall and says to reference it in the body footer; the three commit subjects (bfcd07d8, 6ebfb62f, aa58145e) carry (EPMCDME-16734) as a suffix.
findings.impact: Documented commit-format standard not met; same format feeds the squash-merge title.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subjects to drop the (EPMCDME-16734) suffix and put the ticket key in the body footer, or confirm the PR title follows the documented format.
findings.check_notes: commit history not changed; no fix evidence mapped

disposition.rationale: Repo squash-merges PRs and the ticket branch must not be rebased; commit subjects are rewritten at squash time and the ticket key goes in the PR title/body footer. User approved leaving it.

standards_review.notes: 3 subjects match <type>(<scope>): <subject> with allowed scopes cli and skills; but each appends the ticket key (EPMCDME-16734) to the subject, which git-workflow.md pitfalls say to put in the body footer instead

code-quality.md says functions under 50 lines; createProjectsSubcommand() in src/cli/commands/sdk/projects.ts spans about lines 149-442. Imports use .js, exports have explicit return types, file is under 500 lines, no console.log debug output, no any.

No hardcoded secrets, no credential or header logging, no attribution header changes. File paths for bulk-assign and csv commands come from the invoking user's own CLI args, not an untrusted boundary.

final_round.rationale: Acceptance AC6 is partial (skill Step 4 exempts non-admin projects listed in applications from exists, contradicting the spec) and two blocking standards findings stand (ticket key in commit subjects; createProjectsSubcommand ~290 lines). 7 edge-case candidates dismissed (403 exit 1 is spec AC5; others are input hardening the server already rejects with a shown error); AC9 build evidence is pending-stage-7.
